title: Keep board minutes on cadence
summary: Keep the corporate record clean: schedule the board cadence, prep the minutes template, record the meeting, route minutes for signature, and file them in the data room.

parts.title: Schedule the board cadence
parts.guidance: Plan meetings around upcoming board decisions, available reporting and director attendance. Check the governing documents, investor commitments and jurisdiction-specific obligations for the actual company before choosing the cadence. Include preparation dates for materials and a way to handle urgent decisions through the appropriate special-meeting or written-action process.

parts.title: Prepare the minutes template
parts.guidance: Adapt the company’s prior minutes format to the agenda. Provide places for attendance, notice or waivers, conflicts, motions, votes and referenced materials where relevant. Include proposed resolutions as proposals and leave actual deliberations and outcomes blank. Check that the format fits this entity and meeting type before using it to record the meeting.

parts.title: Hold the meeting and take minutes
parts.guidance: Record who attended, what was considered and what was decided. Capture approved resolutions, voting outcomes, conflicts and assigned actions accurately without inventing a transcript. Use recording or transcription only under the agreed participant arrangements. Compare the draft with the chair’s notes and supporting materials, and resolve disputed recollections before the minutes are approved.

parts.title: Circulate minutes for signature
parts.guidance: Follow the company’s applicable approval and signature process for these minutes. Resolve corrections, freeze the final wording and confirm the required signers and their capacities before sending an approved signature request. Track approval separately from signature completion and keep the execution evidence with the minutes. The correct process may not require every director to sign.

parts.title: File signed minutes in the data room
parts.guidance: File the approved minutes, approval or signature evidence and referenced exhibits in the corporate records. Label them by meeting and keep amendments or follow-up resolutions linked without replacing the original. Restrict access appropriately and check that the records custodian can retrieve the files. Apply the entity’s retention requirements and any legal hold.

geoNotes.summary: Cadence is law, not hygiene: the first board meeting within 30 days of incorporation and at least four a year (gap ≤ 120 days), run per ICSI Secretarial Standard SS-1 — small companies get a lighter two-meeting regime.

No statutory meeting cadence for private companies, but the Companies Act requires minutes of every board and shareholder decision kept for TEN years — written resolutions are the routine substitute for meetings.

metadata.supportReason: Scheduling, templates, signature routing, and filing are automatable. The minutes themselves record human deliberation in the room.
